claim: Initial scan shows only SSH;  fixing the netforge-support service permission issue (chgrp + restart) exposes port 8080 with /health and /diagnose endpoints.
proves: The web service was failing due to permission error; fixing it exposes port 8080 and the /diagnose endpoint.
does_not_prove: Does not prove endpoint is vulnerable
disposition: Multiple enumerations shows only two exists.

claim: /health is not exploitable; only the host parameter on /diagnose allows command injection.
proves: The host parameter is vulnerable to command injection; /health and other parameters are not.
does_not_prove: /health endpoint does not have a vulnerability; could be SQLi
disposition: Output is filtered, only ‘host’ enabled injection.

claim: Command injection is used to create ~support/.ssh, write a public SSH key, and successfully log in as the support user.
proves: We can execute file system commands remotely and establish persistent SSH access as support.
does_not_prove: Command injection may not be the only foothoold
alternative_considered: Could have used reverse shell or other method

claim: sudo -l shows support can run /usr/local/sbin/support-backup as root without password; the script uses tar on /srv/support/uploads without --no-checkpoint, allowing filename‑based command injection.
proves: There is a sudo misconfiguration allowing privilege escalation, and the tar script is vulnerable to filename‑based command injection.
does_not_prove: Does not indicate we are root; we create a SUID shell as payload.

claim: Payload creates a SUID shell at /tmp/rootshell; executing it with -p gives effective root (euid=0); Python is used to setuid(0) and spawn a full root shell.
proves: We have a fully functional root shell.
